findings.F1: The next-day reversal of a vol-scaled daily move appears only when 20-day volatility stands high against its own recent level (20-day vol over its 60-day mean). In the top tercile the slope of next-day excess return on the day's z-score is −51.8 bps per unit (t −3.70, n 987), against +1.4 bps (t 0.12) and −0.5 bps (t −0.04) in the lower two terciles. Pooled, the interaction z × relative-vol is −112.7 bps (t −6.73) and z alone is +104.1 bps (t 5.37), so the reversal grows with the volatility expansion.
findings.F2: Ranking volatility per coin over the whole record gives the same gradient. The z-slope is −69.7 bps (t −5.82, n 1612) in the top volatility tercile, −0.5 bps (t −0.06) in the middle and +15.3 bps (t 2.15) in the bottom. Next-day excess return after the lowest z quintile is +107.6 bps in high vol against −26.7 bps in low vol. The thresholds in this split are look-ahead, so it is supporting only.
findings.F3: The reversal lasts one day only. On non-overlapping grids the z-slope is +7.35 bps (t 0.69, n 2403) at 2 days, −0.0002 (t −0.13, n 1571) at 3 days and 0.0001 (t 0.05, n 947) at 5 days.
findings.F4: A wide high-low range on an up day (range in units of 20-day volatility) is followed by a lower next day. Controlling for z, the range slope on up days is −43.1 bps per unit (t −3.16, n 2445), against +10.6 bps (t 0.96, n 2389) on down days. Over all bars it is −2.6 bps (t −0.45).
findings.F5: The pooled one-day reversal is uneven across coins and years. The z-slope is −21.4 bps (t −2.44) for ETH and −11.2 bps (t −1.62) for BTC. It is −55.8 bps (t −2.98) in 2020, but +10.0 bps (t 0.62) in 2022 and +8.1 bps (t 0.67) in 2024.
findings.F6: The book earns mostly from its long side, and BTC shorts lose. BTC long bars average +6.2 bps (n 1393) and BTC short bars −2.1 bps (n 1478); ETH shorts average +2.5 bps (n 1474). The book's mean daily return is 1.2 bps while holding the coins earned more, so its Sharpe is 0.38 below holding's.
findings.F7: The book's worst 5% of days (n 290) come after the coin rose 43.8 bps the day before, and are followed by a +96.0 bps coin day. The best 5% come after a −54.7 bps day and are followed by −24.2 bps. The book's large days sit inside alternating up and down swings.
findings.F8: No weekday stands out once seven were tested. Wednesday returns average 41.5 bps (t 2.66, n 692), the strongest of the seven, and the same weekday by year is negative in 2018 (−49.9 bps) and 2022 (−12.3 bps).

ideas.idea: The more a coin's 20-day daily volatility stands above its own average of the past 60 days, the more strongly its next 1 day reverses the day's move measured in units of 20-day volatility: up after large falls, down after large rises.
ideas.consequence: A trader should fade outsized daily moves for one day only while volatility is expanding against its recent norm, sizing the fade by that expansion, and refuse the fade when volatility is at or below its recent norm.
ideas.name: vol-expansion one-day reversal

ideas.idea: The wider a coin's rising day's high-low range is in units of its 20-day volatility, the more the coin falls over the next 1 day.
ideas.consequence: A trader can lean short for one day after an up day with an unusually wide range, and refuse to chase such days.
ideas.name: wide-range up-day giveback
